ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Under suitable conditions such as illumination, a certain plant cultivated in an environment with a CO2 concentration of 1% is rapidly transferred to an environment with a CO2 concentration of 0.003%. The changing trends of the micromolar concentrations of C3 and C5 compounds in the dark reaction of its leaves are shown in the figure. Answer the question: is substance A in the figure a C3 compound or a C5 compound?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the vertical axis is “relative concentration,” and the horizontal axis is “time/s.” The dashed line is located at about 200 s; the left side of the dashed line is labeled 1% CO2, and the right side is labeled 0.003% CO2, indicating that the environmental CO2 concentration suddenly decreases at this time. Curve A has a relatively high relative concentration before the dashed line and is basically stable, and after the dashed line it generally shows a downward trend; curve B has a relatively low relative concentration before the dashed line and is stable, and after the dashed line it rises rapidly and then falls back somewhat. Then reason: in the dark reaction of the Calvin cycle, CO2 combines with C5 compounds to form C3 compounds. After the CO2 concentration suddenly decreases, the rate of CO2 fixation decreases, and the formation of C3 compounds decreases, so the C3 concentration decreases; at the same time, the consumption of C5 compounds decreases, so they will relatively accumulate and increase. In the figure, A decreases after CO2 decreases, so A corresponds to the C3 compound.
